title: How to Write a Two-Page CV That Doesn't Bore Nigerian Recruiters
excerpt: Master the art of crafting compelling two-page CVs that grab Nigerian recruiters' attention and land you interviews in today's competitive job market.
author: ElevateResume

body.text: In Nigeria's competitive job market, your CV has just 6-10 seconds to make a lasting impression on recruiters. While the debate between one-page and two-page CVs continues globally, Nigerian employers generally expect comprehensive two-page CVs that showcase your qualifications, experience, and potential value to their organization.

However, length doesn't guarantee quality. Many Nigerian job seekers make the mistake of filling two pages with irrelevant information, outdated formatting, or repetitive content that puts recruiters to sleep. The key is creating a two-page CV that's both comprehensive and engaging.

Nigerian recruiters, whether at companies like Dangote Group, GTBank, or emerging fintech startups like Paystack, receive hundreds of applications daily. They're looking for CVs that quickly communicate:

Unlike Western markets where one-page CVs are preferred for junior roles, Nigerian employers expect detailed information about your background, including personal details, educational history, and comprehensive work experience.
Your two-page CV should follow a strategic layout that prioritizes the most important information on page one while using page two to provide supporting details.

items: Most recent and relevant work experience (2-3 positions)
Education (if you're a recent graduate) or professional certifications

body.text: Always ensure that if a recruiter only reads page one, they get a complete picture of your current professional status and core qualifications.
Your professional summary sets the tone for your entire CV. Nigerian recruiters appreciate summaries that immediately establish your value proposition.
Instead of generic statements like "Hardworking professional seeking opportunities," try:

"Results-driven Marketing Manager with 5+ years experience growing brand awareness for FMCG companies in Lagos. Increased market share by 23% at PZ Cussons through innovative digital campaigns. Expertise in brand management, consumer research, and cross-functional team leadership."

items: Specifies your role and experience level
References a recognizable Nigerian company context

body.text: The work experience section often determines whether recruiters continue reading or move to the next candidate. Here's how to make yours stand out:
Structure your achievements using Situation, Task, Action, Result:

"Led digital transformation project (Situation) to modernize customer service operations (Task) by implementing CRM software and training 15 staff members (Action), resulting in 40% faster response times and 25% increase in customer satisfaction scores (Result)."
Recruiters connect better with experiences they understand. Reference:

items: Local market conditions ("Navigated forex challenges during 2016 recession")
Nigerian business practices ("Managed relationships with distributors across 6 states")
Local competitors or partners ("Secured partnership with Jumia for e-commerce expansion")

body.text: Many Nigerian CVs feature generic skills lists that add no value. Instead, create a skills section that directly relates to your target role:
List specific software, platforms, or technical competencies relevant to Nigerian businesses:
Education remains crucial in the Nigerian job market. Structure this section to highlight:

items: Degree type and field of study
Class of degree (if First Class or Second Class Upper)

body.text: Highlight certifications that add value in the Nigerian context:

items: Online courses from recognized platforms (Coursera, edX, LinkedIn Learning)

Visual appeal matters, but professionalism comes first. Nigerian recruiters prefer clean, organized formats over flashy designs.

items: Use professional fonts: Calibri, Arial, or Times New Roman

body.text: Different sectors in Nigeria have varying expectations for CVs:

items: Emphasize analytical skills and attention to detail
Highlight compliance and risk management experience
Focus on safety certifications and training
Include links to portfolios or GitHub profiles
Mention agile methodologies and project management

body.text: Common Mistakes That Kill Nigerian CVs
Avoid cramming every experience into your CV. Focus on relevance over comprehensiveness.
Remove experiences from over 10-15 years ago unless highly relevant. Update your skills section regularly.
Customize your CV for each application. Use keywords from job descriptions naturally throughout your content.
Typos and grammatical errors immediately disqualify many candidates. Have others review your CV before submitting.
While Nigerian CVs traditionally include personal information, limit this to relevant details like languages spoken or willingness to relocate.
Many Nigerian companies now use ATS software to screen applications initially. Ensure your CV is ATS-friendly:

items: Save in both Word and PDF formats
Test your CV through online ATS checkers
Read aloud to catch awkward phrasing
Verify all dates and company names
Check that contact information is current
Confirm the CV tells a coherent career story
Ask trusted colleagues to review for clarity

body.text: With limited space, every word must serve a purpose. Use:

items: Strong action verbs (achieved, implemented, optimized, streamlined)
Concise phrases over full sentences where appropriate

body.text: Print your CV and review it on paper. Sometimes formatting issues or content problems are more obvious in hard copy format.

Your two-page CV should tell the story of a professional who understands the Nigerian business environment while possessing the skills and experience to drive organizational success. Remember, the goal isn't just to list your qualifications—it's to demonstrate how those qualifications translate into value for potential employers.

By following these guidelines and adapting them to your specific industry and career level, you'll create a two-page CV that not only avoids boring recruiters but actively engages them and compels them to schedule that crucial interview call.
